subject: humanities
passage: The bronze sculptures produced in southern India under the Chola dynasty, between roughly the ninth and thirteenth centuries, were cast by the lost-wax method: an artist modeled the figure in wax, encased it in clay, and melted the wax away so that molten metal could fill the hollow. Because the clay mold had to be broken to free the bronze, and because each casting required a newly modeled wax figure, every piece was ______. Scholars who catalog these works therefore treat apparent near-duplicates not as copies from a shared mold but as separate creations by artists following a common set of conventions.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The text gives two reasons that no mold could be reused: the mold was broken and each casting needed a new wax model. The next sentence confirms that near-duplicates are "not copies from a shared mold but separate creations." The blank must mean "impossible to reproduce exactly."
explanation.A: Correct. Since every mold was destroyed and every wax model was new, each bronze could not be produced again in identical form.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Derivative" means copied from something else, the opposite of what the text says about separate creations rather than copies.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Provisional" means temporary or not yet final; nothing suggests the finished bronzes were temporary.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Many old sculptures are by unknown artists, but the text's reasons (the broken mold, the new wax figure) explain why each piece was one of a kind, not why its maker is unknown.
